beats.say: You think Cleopatra vanished after Antony's defeat, but she vanished a decade earlier, fleeing Rome.
In 30 BC she disguised herself as a priestess, boarding a merchant ship bound for Alexandria's hidden harbor.
beats.visual: map of Mediterranean trade routes 30 BC

beats.say: There she met the young Egyptian mathematician-astronomer Hemiunu, who whispered rumors of a secret tomb beneath the palace.
The tomb, carved from pink limestone, housed a golden sarcophagus inscribed with her true title, "Queen of the Nile".
Roman agents, fearing her diplomatic leverage, set fire to the entrance in 27 BC, sealing the chamber forever.
Centuries later, 1798 explorers uncovered the charred doorway while mapping the Nile's delta, but the sarcophagus vanished again.
Modern satellite imagery in 2021 revealed a rectangular void beneath the ruins of the Royal Quarter, matching ancient sketches.
beats.visual: satellite image of Alexandria Royal Quarter 2021

beats.say: Archaeologists now suspect Cleopatra's real burial site lies not in Alexandria's museum, but hidden in that void.
If recovered, the golden queen could rewrite history, showing she ruled Egypt alone, not as Antony's puppet.
beats.visual: portrait of Cleopatra alone on throne

beats.say: So the next expedition may finally bring Cleopatra home, and the world will finally hear her true voice.
